Verified vulnerability fixes (×2)


    


            

              

                
Local file upload validation and browser-executable inline serving

                verified
              

              

                
Reproduction

                
Before: run pnpm security:probe -- --probe input-file-upload-size-mismatch --run-id before-file-size and pnpm security:probe -- --probe input-file-serve-headers --run-id before-file-headers. The first accepted mismatched bytes; the second served uploaded HTML with inline Content-Disposition.

                
Fix applied

                
api/src/routes/files.ts now rejects local-upload bodies whose byte length differs from files.size_bytes and serves user uploads as attachments with sanitized filenames while retaining X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

                
Proof

                

                  
Before reports: my-docs/evidence/security-audit/runs/before-file-size/report.json and my-docs/evidence/security-audit/runs/before-file-headers/report.json. After reports: my-docs/evidence/security-audit/runs/after-file-size/report.json and my-docs/evidence/security-audit/runs/after-file-headers-2/report.json. Final full report: my-docs/evidence/security-audit/latest.json.


                

              

            

            

              

                
WebSocket malformed/oversized frame resilience

                verified
              

              

                
Reproduction

                
Before: run pnpm security:probe -- --probe websocket-malformed-frame --run-id before-ws-malformed. The probe reported unsafe malformed-frame handling; the first full probe attempt also exposed an unhandled ws oversized-frame error in the dev server log.

                
Fix applied

                
api/src/collaboration/index.ts now catches collaboration message decode failures, closes unsupported/invalid collaboration and events messages with 1003, and handles oversized ws frames with 1009 without crashing the API process.

                
Proof

                

                  
Before report: my-docs/evidence/security-audit/runs/before-ws-malformed/report.json. After reports: my-docs/evidence/security-audit/runs/after-ws-malformed/report.json, my-docs/evidence/security-audit/runs/after-ws-oversized/report.json, and final deterministic close-code evidence in my-docs/evidence/security-audit/latest.json.

Explicit non-claims

          
  • Does not claim remote production penetration testing.
  • Does not claim capability-scoped API tokens beyond the verified super-admin route denial check.
  • Does not claim future dependency advisories will remain zero without rerunning pnpm security:probe.
  • Remote/deployed destructive probing remains out of scope by default; remote mode requires explicit --allow-write and --allow-stress.
  • Created local probe records are retained unless a future run uses cleanup support.
  • Input sanitization probes sample the major current user-facing write/read surfaces and should be extended when new fields are introduced.
  • This is black-box plus assisted review evidence, not a formal external penetration test.

Explicit Non-Claims

          

        

          
Cat 1: Type Safety

          
    
            
  • Does not claim production counted syntax alone clears the 25% threshold.
  • Does not claim all syntax categories carry equal semantic risk.
  • Does not claim every untyped callback parameter has been eliminated.
    • 
          

        

        

          
Cat 2: Bundle Size

          
    
            
  • Does not claim total bundle reduction.
  • Does not claim every large async chunk is optimized.
    • 
          

        

        

          
Cat 3: API Response Time

          
    
            
  • Does not claim rate limiting was weakened in production.
  • Does not claim every measured endpoint improved.
  • Does not claim the large-fixture current benchmark is before/after proof by itself.
  • Does not claim payload-byte reduction alone is equivalent to P95 latency improvement.
    • 
          

        

        

          
Cat 4: Database Query Efficiency

          
    
            
  • Does not claim row-level N+1 was fixed.
  • Does not claim Cat 3 latency improvement from Cat 4 evidence.
    • 
          

        

        

          
Cat 5: Test Coverage and Quality

          
    
            
  • Does not claim zero retry artifacts under every worker count.
  • Does not claim code coverage percentage improved.
  • Does not count stale selector cleanup as one of the three meaningful regression tests.
    • 
          

        

        

          
Cat 6: Runtime Error and Edge Case Handling

          
    
            
  • Does not count comments authorization hardening as a Category 6 user-facing runtime proof.
  • Does not count migration runner hardening as a Category 6 proof.
  • Does not claim every possible component error-boundary gap is fixed; only the route boundary and targeted optional-surface islands are covered.
    • 
          

        

        

          
Cat 7: Accessibility Compliance

          
    
            
  • Does not claim Lighthouse 100.
  • Does not claim full manual keyboard/screen-reader certification.
    • 
          

        

        

          
Cat 8: Security Audit

          
    
            
  • Does not claim remote production penetration testing.
  • Does not claim capability-scoped API tokens beyond the verified super-admin route denial check.
  • Does not claim future dependency advisories will remain zero without rerunning pnpm security:probe.
    •
